title: MAX disruption derepresses nucleolar, Stag3/ncPRC1.6, and Per/Cry clock branches that MYC/MYCN do not mimic
exact_observed_result: Max perturbation produced 167 FDR<0.05 gene-by-cell rows across six Max-tested cell types, including repeated nucleolar/biosynthetic induction, Stag3 induction, and Per2/Cry1 induction. Mga partially shared the Stag3/Obscn branch, while Mnt, Myc, Mycn, E2f1, E2f4, E2f5, Tfdp1, and Tfdp2 failed to induce Stag3 in 151 TH and 155 MB Glut.
biological_interpretation: The neuronal Max signature is more consistent with release of repressive MAX branches, including an MGA/ncPRC1.6-associated meiotic branch and an E-box clock branch, than with simple loss of MYC-driven ribosome biogenesis.

support.description: Max induced the Stag3 and Per/Cry branches, and Mga shared the Stag3 branch in 151 and 155.
Max drove a larger nucleolar/biosynthetic state and the Stag3 branch was absent after MYC/MYCN/E2F-DP perturbations.

caveats: Max mRNA itself was not FDR-depleted and showed mixed log fold-change signs, so the response should be interpreted as a Max-locus perturbation rather than a clean measured Max RNA loss.
MAX/MGA whole-transcriptome similarity was weak even when their Stag3 branch overlapped.

prior_expectation.summary: MAX is the obligatory bHLHZip partner in MYC/MAX and MXD/MNT/MGA repressor networks; MAX and MGA can repress germline or meiosis genes, and MAX has been reported to repress E-box circadian promoters.
